newsitem.title: CANADA: UGG says Pools' bid "totally inadequate".
newsitem.headline: UGG says Pools' bid "totally inadequate".

text.p: A C$172 million hostile takeover bid for United Grain Growers Ltd at C$13.75 a share is "totally inadequate," UGG chief executive Brian Hayward told Reuters.
"The board consulted with its financial and legal advisers and the price is totally inadequate," Hayward said in a telephone interview.

Alberta Wheat Pool and Manitoba Pool Elevators on Thursday unveiled a C$13.75 a share bid for all remaining outstanding common voting shares in UGG, citing the threat of a U.S. multinational takeover of the grain handling company.
UGG shares soared to an all-time high of C$14.25 Thursday.
The cooperatives, which already owned 14.98 percent of UGG's shares through a joint holding company, said that company had a lock-up agreement to buy another 6.4 percent.
"We don't know of any other bid because there've been statements about them doing this to keep UGG Canadian, so we're not aware of any other pending bid," Hayward said.
Persistent rumors have said Nebraska-based ConAgra Inc or Illinois-based Archer Daniels Midland Co were interested in buying UGG. Officials at both firms were not available for comment.
Saskatchewan Wheat Pool was also rumored to be interested in UGG. SWP said it is an "interested observer."
The pools' offer, due to expire March 27, requires the removal of UGG's shareholder rights plan, or poison pill. The rights plan was adopted by UGG's board of directors Friday.
"We believe, unless they can prove it to the contrary, we believe that they've triggered the pill," Hayward added.

Hayward said UGG's share surge on the TSE proved the pools' offer was below market expectations and cited Scotia McLeod analyst Steven Holt's buy order issued late Thursday as evidence of the equity market's assessment of the pools' bid.

"We intend to take any and all actions to protect our shareholders' interests and to examine every feasible alternative that may help us fulfill our responsibility to maximize the value of the company to our shareholder," UGG president and chairman Ted Allen said in a statement.
UGG retained Scotia CApital Markets and Davies, Ward & Beck as its financial and legal advisers on the pools' bid.
